item.title: Re: The Boy Who Can Do Anything (Looking For Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
You typed that the dog was there to apparently defuse the kid; how does he do that?

The problem is simply that the kid feels more like a MacGuffin than an actual character: There's a problem, the kid shows up, problem solved, if he gets out of hand a dog shows up to slow him down.

We already have that in SCP-343 (assuming He's who He says he is); but that character is still a character. We need some way of differentiating this guy from any other MacGuffin and that's usually through its personality.

This guy needs a lot of work, but if you can start with the personality and go from there it should be a lot easier for you.

item.title: Re: The Boy Who Can Do Anything (Looking For Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
Not a critter but a fellow writer with some concerns and suggestions.

Your idea is a bit basic and amateurish. This boy is very overpowered and the only drawback is fatigue he also has a magic dog that ensures his safety and the continuous effect of his powers, there isn't really anything that makes us care or worry about him so far. It lacks balance.
Giving limits or severe consequences or prices to his powers is a way to make him a more interesting and likeable character. Maybe by using his powers he damages or affects the people whose faith enable him to use them. Maybe he can only do the miracles described on the Bible (turn water into wine, walk over the water, revive the dead, cure sickness), it is a clear limitation and ties nicely to the Christian theme. Maybe he shortens his own life by using the powers. Something that makes the use of the powers to be a difficult choice and not a menial task.
Also, you stated that the powers were given by God but He is not know for giving powers to people just because. Why was he given these powers? Is there a divine task for him to fulfill? Did his parents make a ritual or offering? Is it really God who gifted him the powers or was it something else posing as God?

Please don't be discouraged by my questions, with proper balancing and a strong narrative arc I'm sure you will be able to pull this off.

item.title: Re: The Boy Who Can Do Anything (Looking For Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
1) Lots of ideas, but there's nothing solid here. There's no real narrative, nothing really bringing it together. We need a story, not just your outline.

2) If he gains power from Christian belief, then how does converting everyone to Christianity negate his ability?

3) There's just no real hook here, no reason to care. It's a neat idea, but there's just nothing really here. You have the barest of skeletons here, but there's just no muscle or even skin. Give us some details!

item.title: The Boy Who Can Do Anything (Looking For Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
He will be able to do anything mentally (using the tulpa effect) and will experience extreme effects after. He can only use his ability from other Christians. He was given this ability from god (hence the Christianity). His dog will come after the effects as a defence and will emit a memetic effect converting anyone who views it to Christianity so the boy can still use his effect. More in pitch. (First time writing, already writ most of it asking off of reddit, sorry! I will post the draft later.)

I've trimmed your thread summary as it was very lengthy. Please keep it down to 1-3 lines to prevent taking up space on the forums. —RockTeethMothEyes

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Religious History

Page Layout: Get the fairly long containment procedure out the way then the SCP then his effects and SCP-xxxx-1A/B's effects, Discovery, His unique procedure , Interviews and maybe missions.

Elevator Pitch:The SCP can do anything mentally with The Tulpa Effect, but only from Christian minds. This leads to fatigue and -1A will come. -1A is a big dog with supernatural features. When he comes, an effect known as -1B happens, -1B will make anyone viewing convert to Christianity. This is a fail safe for his ability.

Central Narrative: He can save the world if any K-Class end of the world scenario occurs. God gave the ability.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:Descriptive word choices, depth in ability.

Additional Notes:Human speech, Mission scenarios.
